method.method_draft: Use a direct angle-complement argument. From the image, identify that angle 3 is the angle at C between ray CG and segment CB. Also read the right-angle marker at B, showing CB is perpendicular to the diagonal line AG, with B lying on AG. From the text, use m∠AGC = 40°, which is the angle between GA and GC. Since CB is perpendicular to GA, the angle between CB and GC is the complement of the angle between GA and GC. Therefore, m∠3 = 90° - 40° = 50°. The given m∠DGF = 53° is not needed for this route.

method.method_draft: Use an orientation/coordinate-bearings setup. From the image, take ray GC as the positive horizontal direction from G to C. The text says m∠AGC = 40°, so ray GA is oriented 40° above GC. The right-angle marker at B shows CB is perpendicular to AG, and the diagram shows CB goes from C up-left toward B, so from C its direction is 40° + 90° = 130° from the positive horizontal. Ray CG from C points left, i.e. 180° from the positive horizontal. Thus angle 3, between CB and CG at C, is 180° - 130° = 50°. The 53° angle DGF is unused.
